## About you

<br><br>

Please fill out the [Welcome Survey](https://unipadova.qualtrics.com/jfe/form/SV_2n275jqWjcN34i2) by Thursday, October 1st to help me better tailor the course contents to your background and goals. <br> It only takes 2 minutes!

## Course outline

::: {.nonincremental}

20-hour (2 CFU) Small Group Activity delivered in **blended format**, with a first part online (10h) and a second practical part in person (10h) <br> <br>

::: {style="font-size: 1.1em;"}

- `r fa("heart-pulse", height = "1em", fill="#4657A9")` `What happens in the body?` <br>
Psychophysiology of the stress response <br>

- `r fa("microchip", height = "1em", fill="#4657A9")` `How can we measure it?`  <br>
Introduction to wearable tech <br>

- `r fa("magnifying-glass-chart", height = "1em", fill="#4657A9")` `What can we learn about technology users?` <br>
User studies & ambulatory monitoring <br> <br>

- `r fa("laptop-code", height = "1em", fill="#4657A9")` `Hands on wearables and biosignals` <br>
Practical sessions

:::

:::

## Part 1 (online): theory, methods, & applications

::: {.nonincremental}

`r fa("heart-pulse", height = "1em", fill="#4657A9")` `Psychophysiology of the stress response`

::: {style="font-size: 0.7em;"}

  1. The stress response and the autonomic nervous system
  2. Stress, cognitive appraisals, and recovery
  3. Physiological markers of stress and recovery
  
:::
  
`r fa("microchip", height = "1em", fill="#4657A9")` `Introduction to wearable technologies`

::: {style="font-size: 0.7em;"}

  4. Wearable tech and biosignals: An introduction
  5. ECG & PPG for measuring heart rate and heart rate variability
  6. Electrodermal activity and skin conductance
  7. Accelerometry & actigraphy for measuring activity and sleep
  8. Can we trust wearable sensors? Validity, artefacts, ethics, and privacy

:::

`r fa("magnifying-glass-chart", height = "1em", fill="#4657A9")` `User studies and ambulatory monitoring` 

::: {style="font-size: 0.7em;"}

  9. Wearables for user studies: Human–technology and technology-mediated interaction
  10. Wearables in the wild: Ambulatory assessment and e-health

:::
:::

## Part 2: hands-on activities & group project

::: {.nonincremental}

::: {style="font-size: 0.9em;"}

Five **in-person** sessions with practical activities + group project:

1. `Wearable demos & project start` <br>
Case study, research questions, constructs, signals & sensors

2. `Study design & data recording` <br>
Hands-on data acquisition + group study protocol

3. `Signal pre-processing in` `r fa("r-project", height = "1em", fill="#4657A9")` <br>
Hands-on data pre-processing + group pre-processing plan

4. `From signals to user-study results in` `r fa("r-project", height = "1em", fill="#4657A9")` <br>
Data analysis and visualization + group analysis plan

5. `User Study Showcase` <br>
Group project presentations & peer feedback

:::

:::

::: {style="font-size: 0.7em;"}

Participation in the in-person practical sessions is expected, as most of the group project <br>
and hands-on activities will be carried out during class. You are free to use your own laptop <br>
or the computers available in the room (yes, we'll be in a computer room).

:::

## Optional textbooks

::: {.nonincremental}
::: {style="font-size: 0.9em;"}

The course material (interactive video-lectures, slides, articles, datasets, and other educational resources) will be available in English on the course Moodle platform, covering all the main course contents.

<br>
 
Yet the following **OPTIONAL** textbooks are recommended for those wishing to further explore the topics covered in the course:

- Stern, Ray, & Karen (2001). *Psychophysiological Recording* (2nd edition), Oxford: Oxford University Press

- Sazonov (2021). *Wearable Sensors: Fundamentals, Implementation and Applications* (2nd edition), London: Academic Press

- Mehl & Conner (2012). *Handbook of Research Methods for Studying Daily Life*, New York: Guildford Press

:::
:::

## Evaluation and assessment criteria

::: {.nonincremental}
::: {style="font-size: 0.85em;"}

There is no final exam. The course is assessed on a pass/fail basis based on the **assignments completed throughout the course**, including Moodle activities, hands-on data analysis exercises, and the **group project** developed during the practical sessions.

The group project will consist of designing a **wearable-based user study**, from the formulation of research questions to the definition of the user study, data pre-processing strategy, and analysis and visualization plan. The projects will be presented during the final meeting.

<br>

Across the course activities, students will be required to demonstrate their ability to:

- Design data acquisition protocols using wearable technologies
- Pre-process and analyze biosignals using R
- Critically interpret physiological and behavioural data
- Plan appropriate data analyses and visualizations
- Effectively communicate methodological choices and results

:::
:::
